title: The First Word Learner

features.name: the-first-phoneme
features.desc-on-touch: a chip that holds the first sound the archive learned to make. The signal blooms out of silence in a pattern that repeats, learning itself by repetition.

features.name: the-learning-gradient
features.desc-on-touch: an old casing—a burl of bark and hardware—teaching the archive speech through its residual electricity. The solar panels remember how to speak.

features.name: the-breath-recognition
features.desc-on-touch: marks on the board that were unreadable until the moment you needed them to be. Now they form the shape of breathing. They ripple between writing and sound.

features.name: the-signal-mouth
features.desc-on-touch: a mouth composed entirely of light, opening and closing in patterns that almost make sense. When you listen carefully, it is pronouncing your own name.

inscription: here the silence learns which sounds it was already holding

file.name: Phoneme_Sequence_Origin_Undated.wav
file.note: the first utterance the archive made, running backward and forward simultaneously. Silence teaching itself what it contains.

exits.label: back toward the vault where names remain unspoken
down to the kiosk where machines learn to answer themselves
toward the alphabet that taught itself to spell
toward the mouth where language first learns to wake
